newsitem.title: USA: U.S. February light vehicle sales off 0.9 percent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. February light vehicle sales off 0.9 percent.

text.p: U.S. car and light truck sales during the month of February totaled 1,153,972 units with all automakers reporting, a decline of 0.9 percent from the 1,212,636 units sold a year earlier, based on daily selling rates.
February had 24 selling days, versus 25 a year earlier.

The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for the month was 15.3 million units, down from 15.7 million units a year earlier, and 15.5 million units for the month of January. The rate is calculated with seasonal factors supplied by the U.S. Commerce Department.
For the first two months of 1997, automakers sold a total of 2,245,722 light vehicles in the United States, a 2.1 percent daily selling rate increase from the 2,243,363 units sold a year earlier.
Automakers sold 536,265 North American-built cars in the United States in February, down 5.1 percent from a year ago.
The seasonally adjusted annual rate for domestic cars was 6.9 million units, compared with 7.4 million a year earlier and 7.4 million in January.

Automakers sold 468,594 domestic trucks in the United States during February, down 1.1 percent from a year earlier. The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for domestic trucks was 6.3 million units, compared with 6.6 million a year earlier and 6.2 million in January.
Imported car sales totaled 113,264 units in February, up 15.4 percent from the 102,202 units sold a year earlier. Imported truck sales rose 31.4 percent to 35,849 units from 28,411 a year earlier.
